kakekotoba.interaction: 世 (yo) is the classic dual-meaning word for 'the world/society' and 'one's life/lot' — here it operates as the object of 思ふ, meaning both 'the world at large' (as a social/political order) and 'my own life/fate' (as the poet's personal circumstance under which he suffers, especially resonant given Gotoba's own exile). The single word carries both the public and the personal register simultaneously.

kigo.note: No genuine seasonal word is present in this poem; 世 (the world/one's life) is a philosophical-existential term, not a seasonal image. The poem is entirely in the register of abstract emotional/ethical reflection (人間不信 and grief over worldly affairs) rather than nature imagery, so season is properly 'none'.

bipartite.kami_theme: A statement of contradictory feelings toward other people — some are dear/beloved (惜し), others are resented (恨めし) — introduced by the exclamation あぢきなく ('how bitter/futile it all is').
bipartite.shimo_theme: The cause of this emotional turmoil is explained: because the speaker broods anxiously over the state of the world (world-weariness, yo), his very being has become one that is perpetually sunk in troubled thought (もの思ふ身).
bipartite.pivot_note: The kami-no-ku presents the raw paradoxical emotional symptom (loving and resenting people at once), and the shimo-no-ku supplies its root cause — obsessive brooding over 世 (the world/his own fate) — collapsing outward social feeling into an interior condition of ceaseless melancholy. The ゆゑに ('because of') explicitly marks the logical-causal turn from symptom to cause, making this a reflective causal pivot rather than an image-based one; there is no natural image mediating the two halves, only introspective reasoning, which is itself a distinguishing feature of this famously abstract, philosophical Shin-kokinshū-style poem.

source_jp:
人も惜し
人も恨めし
あぢきなく
世を思ふゆゑに
もの思ふ身は
